##: NetEase UU accelerator (网易UU加速器) from uu.163.com.

Every download button on the site is a tracking link to adl.netease.com, which renders a landing page holding a signed CDN URL (uu.gdl.netease.com/<release-id>/UU-<version>.exe?key1=...&key2=...). key2 decodes to the issue time plus 12 hours, so that URL cannot be recorded in a manifest.

dl.uu.163.com serves the same object store without the signature: it returns the same Content-Length (43,168,760) and the file's MD5 equals the ETag of the signed CDN copy. It is the slower origin, but it stays valid, so that is what 'url' pins.

The installer is a custom PE stub, not Inno Setup or NSIS: the payload is an LZMA2 7z archive in RCDATA resource 201. 7-Zip descends into that resource, so '#/dl.7z' needs a single pass and yields <release-id>\ (123 files, uu.exe included), uu_launcher.exe, uu_agent.exe, uninstall.exe and VisualElements\.
The release-id directory changes with every build (5256 for 6.23.0), so the installer script locates the directory that holds uu.exe and flattens it instead of hard-coding the name.
checkver reads the adl landing page because it is the only endpoint that carries the new version together with the matching release-id, which autoupdate needs to rebuild the URL.
The shortcut and bin point at uu_launcher.exe, not uu.exe: update.exe relaunches the launcher after an update, so it is the stable entry point, and both binaries request elevation anyway.
The vendor publishes no checksum, so autoupdate has no hash source and the Excavator recomputes the SHA-256 on update.
description: NetEase UU game accelerator (网易UU加速器)
notes: uu.exe and uu_launcher.exe carry a requireAdministrator manifest, so Windows asks for elevation on every start: the accelerator installs a TAP/WFP driver and a Windows service at runtime.
The vendor uninstaller is dropped - it assumes a Program Files layout and its own registry entry - so Scoop owns the uninstall.
Logs are written into the app directory (config.txt sets 'logdir .'), so 'scoop update' clears them; no %APPDATA% or %LOCALAPPDATA% path appears in the payload, so there is nothing to persist.
The bundled updater (update.exe) stays enabled and may replace the app outside Scoop; run 'scoop install uu -f' to return to the packaged build.
